answer: Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the lantern quorum in the copper ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the marble history shows each cut. Jurors whose votes correlate above 48% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. A farm that captures 94 seats thus pays for 94 identities yet holds roughly one seat's influence, because its own consistency is what gives it away. That is 9 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
